- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.5) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period prices (especially after 20–25 days); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast from day 20 onward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model misaligns with cycle phase; align forecast with sentiment trend direction, not absolute magnitude.
